basic_identification.sector_category: Footwear (approved by the Chemical Division Council and finalized by the Footwear Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements, sampling guidelines, and testing methods for Hawai Chappals designed for everyday, light-duty consumer use. It covers footwear manufactured from vulcanized rubber, thermoplastic rubber (TPR), ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA), polyurethane (PU), thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU), or other polymeric materials and their combinations.

amendment_slips.description: Establishes English footwear sizing ranges as per IS 1638; splits adult footwear into Type 1 (uniform sole thickness) and Type 2 (tapered sole design); removes Fig. 2; and permits strap wing thickness to be mutually agreed between manufacturers and buyers.

Substitutes Clause 4 to define Kids vs. Adults categories strictly based on a 220 mm last length threshold [1]; deletes Clause 5 [1]; inserts a mandatory slip-resistance (coefficient of friction) requirement of minimum 0.3 for Adults (Type 1) on quarry tiles [1]; limits Table 2 (iii) heavy metals and chemical markers specifically to PVC strap materials [1]; and completely replaces density calculation formulas under Clause C-2.6 and C-2.7 [1, 2].

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Footwear made from All Rubber and all Polymeric Material and its Components (Quality Control) Order' (QCO 2024) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all Hawai Chappals manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Micro and small scale units are granted specific delayed implementation schedules, and export shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to molded rubber/polymeric footwear.

requirements.detail: Every pair of Hawai Chappals must be legibly and indelibly marked on the outer waist of the sole and the inner face of the straps with the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's licence number (CM/L).

Under Amendment No. 2, footwear size categories are strictly split: a) Kids: Standard English sizes for infants and children up to 220 mm last length; b) Adults: Standard English sizes above 220 mm last length [1].

Adults (Type 1) Hawai Chappals must satisfy a dynamic slip-resistance coefficient of friction (COF) of minimum 0.3 when tested on wet quarry tiles [1]. This test is not applicable to kids' sizes, Adults (Type 2), or if the chappal features a leather sole [1].

The outsole/bottom material must be homogeneous, free from blisters, cavities, or collapses. Key mechanical boundaries include: a) Minimum overall sole thickness: 8.0 mm; b) Bottom density: minimum 0.15 g/cm³; c) Compression set at constant deflection: maximum 50.0%; d) High resistance to abrasion wear and cyclic flex cracking.

The strap must exhibit robust tensile properties: a) Strap-to-strap breaking strength: minimum 30 kg (294 N) at the V-shape junction; b) Toe-post to strap breaking strength: minimum 10 kg (98 N); c) Elongation at break: minimum 250% for solid straps. Under Amendment No. 2, Table 2 (iii) chemical restrictions are applicable specifically to PVC strap materials only [1].
To prevent toxic heavy metal exposure, the lead content of the strap material must be extremely low, not exceeding a strict limit of 2 ppm.

Density is mathematically calculated using the revised formula: Density (g/cm³) = (1 000 * F) / (T * W * L), where F is mass (g), T is average thickness of five readings (mm), W is average of four width measurements (mm), and L is length of the two shorter edges (mm) [1].

Density is mathematically calculated using the revised formula: Density (g/cm³) = (F * 4 000) / (3.14 * [D * D * T]), where F is mass (g), D is average of three diameter readings (mm), and T is average of five thickness readings (mm) [2].

Random roll selection from a lot must conform to Table 3 based on roll quantity: up to 50 rolls (select 3, allowed defectives = 0), 51-150 (select 5, allowed defectives = 0), 151-300 (select 8, allowed defectives = 0), and 301 or more (select 13, allowed defectives = 0) [3].

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 10702 : 2023 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification establishing physical, mechanical, and safety requirements for everyday Hawai Chappals (rubber or polymeric slippers). Under India's statutory Footwear Quality Control Order (QCO), all Hawai Chappals supplied to the domestic market must be certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards and bear the Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Amendment No. 2 (October 2025) introduces critical updates, defining Kids' vs. Adults' footwear sizes based on a 220 mm last length threshold [1] and enforcing a new dynamic slip-resistance requirement of at least 0.3 coefficient of friction (COF) for adult Type 1 slippers [1]. It also mandates high strap-to-strap tensile limits (minimum 30 kg), limits toxic heavy-metal lead content in straps to 2 ppm, and provides highly specific formulas for calculating specimen densities to prevent the blending of low-grade, brittle polymeric fillers [1, 2].
